local_checks.invariant: Any GUI input that can change /workspace outside policy happens inside an open burst that has a restore point, a gui_changes record and a stray-process stop at close.
local_checks.result: Partial source review. Bursts open only via _snapshot when _gui_needs_snapshot is true and close on idle/next_burst/human_takeover/end_desktop. _open_gui_burst, _stop_gui_strays and _close_gui_burst swallow exceptions and return with no audit record, so a failed open/close leaves no trace. Not settled whether container-controlled conditions can trigger those failures.

unresolved: Hunter stopped early. Unsettled: whether container-controlled state can make workspace_manifest or desktop_processes fail at burst open (no burst, so no gui_changes and no stray stop) or at close (no record), after which the next burst treats earlier processes as baseline.

Unsettled: whether images/desktop tooling and autostart/session paths under /home/desktop let changes reach /workspace with no open burst, including after snapshot restore. Needs a parent-led images/desktop review and a live desktop-image check.

local_checks.invariant: Agent tool calls run on a dedicated pool separate from human API threads, and per-sandbox tool_concurrency bounds how many pool threads one sandbox can hold
local_checks.result: api.py:81 creates a 32-thread tool_pool used only by POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool} (api.py:206-211). service.py:274-278 enforces 4 concurrent calls per sandbox (429 beyond) and decrements in finally (288-290). One sandbox can hold at most 4 of 32 pool threads; saturating the pool takes 8 or more sandboxes acting together (aggregate, not a single-principal bypass). Approved actions run on the human request thread (service.py:414-415, Starlette threadpool), and exec there is bounded by timeout -k 5 exec_timeout (sandbox.py:531).

local_checks.invariant: Work done on behalf of sandbox B is charged to B's tool_concurrency and never runs on another sandbox's or a human's request thread
local_checks.result: Mocked harness in sbx: with an idle open GUI burst for sbB, sbA's call_tool('list_dir') ran sbB's workspace_manifest on sbA's thread (manifest calls [('sbB','sbA-request')], elapsed 0.50s = stub delay) while _busy only shows sbA. expire_stale() (reached from GET/POST approvals and decide) ran the same sbB close on the human thread (0.50s). service.py:273 calls close_idle_gui_bursts() before the busy check, and it iterates every sandbox's bursts (service.py:250-256).

local_checks.invariant: Every docker exec reached from the burst-close and GUI paths has a deadline
local_checks.result: Of the execs, only exec (sandbox.py:531), read_file (561) and outbox_read (665) carry a timeout. workspace_manifest (499), desktop_processes ps and xdotool (689-691), kill_processes (697), and the _x GUI calls (683-684, used by click/type/key/screenshot/geometry) use exec_run with no timeout, and the docker SDK exec_run has no deadline parameter. Whether container state can actually keep these execs from returning is runtime behaviour, not visible in source.

x_hardening: tool_pool (32) / tool_concurrency (4) means 8 or more cooperating sandboxes can occupy every tool thread for up to exec_timeout+5 s per call; human routes run on the separate Starlette pool, so the effect is limited to other agents' tool latency. Consider a global cap tied to the pool size or a fair queue.

Client disconnect does not cancel tool_pool work (api.py:209 run_in_executor); bounded for exec by its timeout, but the untimed execs listed above have no such bound. Add a deadline to every container exec (e.g. wrap in timeout as exec does).

snapshot_quota counts human manual and import snapshots toward the agent's quota (sandbox.py:503-505 counts all rows). That is conservative, but it can push an agent into approval mode earlier than the operator expects.

local_checks.invariant: Every route enforces the right principal kind and binds the action to the right resource; agent header tokens are confined to their own sandbox; browser cookie sessions reach only screen_principal routes.
local_checks.result: principal() (api.py:92-101) accepts only an Authorization: Bearer header, so cookies never drive the JSON management API. human_only (103-106) blocks agents. Agent-reachable routes re-bind the resource to the token's sandbox: GET /sandboxes/{sid} (161-164), POST /tools/{tool} (206-208), GET /approvals/{aid} (226-230; agents get id/status/result/decided_at for their own sandbox only), GET /desktop/state (316-318). POST /approvals/{aid} rejects agents with 403 and audits it (242-249). screen_human requires scope '*' (126-132), desktop_human scope in ('*',sid) (134-140); both re-check kind=='human'. No weaker parallel path found; log_human-before-validate on pause/resume/snapshot/restore/delete is human-only and only appends an audit row for a bad sid.

local_checks.invariant: A sandbox-scoped ticket/session cannot become a '*' session, and a scope=A session cannot act on sandbox B or '*' routes (fix for the prior rejected claim).
local_checks.result: redeem binds ticket scope to the requested sid (desktop.py:105-114); new_session persists scope (116-125); session()/session_scope() gate on scope in ('*',sid) (133-152). Harness: scope='sbxA' ticket redeemed as '*' -> None; as 'sbxA' -> scope-A session; that session's session(cookie,None) and session(cookie,'sbxB') -> None, session(cookie,'sbxA') ok; '*' ticket valid everywhere; reuse -> None.

local_checks.invariant: All /ui/* routes authorize as a full-UI human; sandbox pages need a '*' session.
local_checks.result: browser_human=screen_human (api.py:437); every /ui/* data route depends on it (web.py:157,161,176,200,204,217,228,232,241,252,260,266). Pages /, /ui, /ui/sandboxes/{sid} gate on session(cookie,None) requiring '*' (web.py:82-83,106,152,183). /login ticket path redeems only '*' tickets (111). POST /login and /logout enforce same_origin (118,130).

local_checks.invariant: The record returned to an agent for its own sandbox does not leak a stronger principal's secret.
local_checks.result: get()/list() strip token_hash (sandbox.py:318-333); token plaintexts never returned. get() returns host source_dir path, container_id, image, runtime to the agent (hardening only: network=none, no exfil path, same value shown to the human by design).
